chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who acknowledged to an inheritor of his, and he was ill, with a debt being upon him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is allowed for him (to pay off), when he acknowledge with it, besides the third'.

key_terms.مَرِيضٌ: ill/sick (specifically in the context of deathbed)

ai.seo_question: Can a dying person acknowledge a debt to one of their heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that a dying person's acknowledgment of debt to an heir is valid without requiring the consent of other heirs, provided the amount does not exceed one-third of the estate. This ruling distinguishes between bequest (wasiyyah) and debt recognition, ensuring the financial rights of the deceased are settled fairly within the limits of testamentary freedom recognized in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who acknowledge to an inheritor of his, and he was ill, with a debt being upon him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is allowed for him (to pay off), when he acknowledge with it, besides the third’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from ’Isma‘il ibn Jabir who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who confirms in his illness his owing a certain amount of debts to one of his heirs. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible if the amount is less than one-third of the legacy.’”
